title: `.env` is regenerated from the manifest on demand; the file is never authoritative
asA: developer with local tooling that expects a `.env`
iWant: a reflector command that fills `.env` from the manifest
soThat: my local flow keeps working without the `.env` becoming the source of truth

acceptanceCriteria.description: Running the reflector writes a `.env` file at the repo root whose keys equal the manifest slice for the target process and whose values equal the current vendor-resolved values for the active environment; a subsequent invocation overwrites the file atomically.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator who has authenticated to the vendor and passed a deployable id and active environment
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs `secrets reflect --deployable <id> --env <env>` and reads the resulting `.env`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file's parsed key set equals the declared slice for `<id>` and every value equals the vendor-resolved value for the active environment; a repeat run atomically replaces the file and no intermediate partial-write state is observable

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project's `.gitignore` at the repo root excludes `.env` (and any `.env.*` reflection variants declared for other environments) from version control.
acceptanceCriteria.when: `git check-ignore .env` runs at the repo root
acceptanceCriteria.then: the command reports `.env` as ignored and exits 0

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CI source-tree scan fails a change that reads `.env` directly at boot instead of going through the Secrets Manager client.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change that adds a call parsing `.env` (a `dotenv.config()`-shaped call outside the Secrets Manager module)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the CI gate runs on the change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run fails with a stable-coded `SECRETS_DOTENV_DIRECT_READ` error naming the offending source path and directing the author to the Secrets Manager client
